   City Council Meeting Agenda

 •  CALL TO ORDER
 •  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE LED BY: Vice Mayor Liao

  Harrington, Pu

 1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

 2. PRESENTATIONS

  A. INTRODUCTION OF PLANNING MANAGER SAMANTHA TEWASART

 4. CONSENT CALENDAR

  All items listed under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and

  City Council or audience requests separate discussion.

  A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  The minutes are a record of the official actions taken at the City Council
  meeting.

  1. Minutes of the City Council Special Meeting of August 4, 2020.

  2. Minutes of the City Council Regular Meeting of August 4, 2020.

  Recommended Action: Approval.

  B. MATERIAL DEMANDS

  This is the presentation of the “Register of Demands and Warrants” for the
  payment of City expenditures.

  Recommended Action: Approval.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – August 18, 2020  2
   C. CASH AND INVESTMENT REPORT – JULY 2020

  This is the presentation of City investments for the month of July 2020.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council receive and file the Cash and
  Investment Report for July 2020.

  D. VEHICLE LEASE WITH THE HOLMAN CAPITAL CORPORATION

  The City Council has provided funding in the 2020-2021 budget for the lease
  purchase of vehicles valued at approximately $636,000 and paid for via annual
  lease payments totaling $110,700. These were approximations based on the
  information available. The departments experiencing immediate need were
  the Police Department, the Fire Department and Public Works.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that City Council:

  1. Authorize the usage of the Holman Capital Corporation for the vehicle
  lease purchase project; and
  2. Authorize the City Manager to execute all related agreements.

  E. ADOPTION OF RESOLUTION NUMBERS 20-36 AND 20-37 SETTING THE
  RATE AND AMOUNT NECESSARY FOR THE 2020-21 FISCAL YEAR
  RETIREMENT LEVY

  The City’s retirement costs are funded by a special property tax levy
  authorized by the voters in 1948. This levy requires the City Council to
  annually establish a tax rate sufficient to meet the City’s obligations to the
  state employees’ retirement system. No change in the tax rate is
  recommended for the 2020-21 Fiscal Year and the City Council is asked to
  confirm the current rate and fix the amount of property taxes to be generated
  by adopting two Resolutions.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 20-36, setting
  the tax rate at 14 cents per $100 assessed valuation, and Resolution No. 20-

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – August 18, 2020  3
   37, fixing the amount of property taxes to be generated for the City’s
  employees’ retirement cost for Fiscal Year 2020-21.

  F. RESOLUTIONS TO EXECUTE CALTRANS AGREEMENTS FOR DEVELOPING
  A LOCAL ROADWAY SAFETY PLAN

  The City was awarded a grant to develop a Local Roadway Safety Plan (LRSP)
  which will identify and prioritize a list of roadway safety improvements within
  the City. A program supplement agreement and an updated master
  agreement must be executed with Caltrans before the City can submit
  invoices for reimbursement of work.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Adopt Resolution No. 20-38 and Resolution No. 20-39; and
  2. Authorize the City Manager to execute the Administering Agency-State
  Master Agreement No. 00517S and Program Supplement Agreement No.
  U97 between the City and Caltrans; and
  3. Authorize the use of up to $72,000 in the account of 124-800-57-96-794
  to be reimbursed by Caltrans.

  G. SAFE, CLEAN WATER PROGRAM (MEASURE W) TRANSFER AGREEMENT

  In order to receive approximately $440,000 from the voter-approved Safe,
  Clean Water Program (Measure W), a Transfer Agreement between the City
  and the Los Angeles County Flood Control District needs to be executed. The
  Agreement will allow the City to receive funding for several stormwater
  projects.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the City Manager to execute
  the Transfer Agreement between the City and the Los Angeles Flood Control
  District.

 5. PUBLIC HEARING – None.

 6. NEW BUSINESS

  A. MONTHLY BUDGET UPDATE

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – August 18, 2020  4
   The City Council unanimously passed the budget for Fiscal Year 2020-2021
  on June 23, 2020. However, due to the staggering economic impacts of
  COVID-19, the City Council requested that the staff conduct a monthly update
  at the regularly-scheduled second meeting of the month. This standing item
  would be for the purposes of bringing any major changes or developments
  to the City Council.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Adopt Resolution No. 20-42 appropriating Gas Tax Funds in the amount
  of $330,000 from Fund balance to 136-800-02-40-003 Utilities – Electricity;
  and
  2. Receive and file this report.

  B. CONSIDERATION BY THE CITY COUNCIL TO ADOPT RESOLUTION NO.
  20-41 CONDEMNING AN ATTEMPT BY THE TRUMP ADMINISTRATION
  TO EXCLUDE UNDOCUMENTED PERSONS FROM THE 2020 CENSUS
  COUNT APPORTIONMENT BASE

  08/18/2020 SEPARATE ATTACHMENT: PROPOSED  CHANGES TO
  RESOLUTION NO. 20-41

  During the August 4, 2020 City Council Meeting, the City Council directed
  staff to prepare a resolution in response to the Memorandum for the
  Secretary of Commerce issued by President Trump dated July 21, 2020,
  “Subject: Excluding Illegal Aliens from the Apportionment Base Following the
  2020 Census.” The City Council will consider adopting Resolution No. 20-41
  responding to the Trump Administration’s recent attempt to exclude persons
  from population counts and apportionment determinations following the
  2020 Census based on citizenship and immigration status.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve Resolution No. 20-41,
  responding to the Trump Administration’s attempt to exclude undocumented
  persons from the 2020 Census Count apportionment base.

  C. STATUS REPORT FROM THE COMMUNITY EQUALITY AND
  ENGAGEMENT AD HOC SUB-COMMITTEE AND RECOMMENDATION TO

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – August 18, 2020  5
   CREATE A COMMISION ON HUMAN EQUITY, ACCESS AND RELATIONS
  (THE “HEAR COMMISSION”)

  In the wake of the killing of George Floyd and the civil unrest that followed,
  the City Council adopted a resolution committing to a process of examination
  and engagement with the community to review the City’s current policies and
  practices to ensure the fair, even and equal administration and enforcement
  of its laws, and to eliminate racism and discrimination in the City of San
  Gabriel’s policies and practices. To start the process, the City Council
  appointed an ad hoc sub-committee (the “Subcommittee”) to hold
  community conversations and begin to formulate a plan for achieving the
  mandates in the resolution. This report presents a summary of the work of the
  Subcommittee and a recommendation to create a Commission on Human
  Equity, Access and Relations (the “HEAR Commission” or the “Commission”)
  to thoroughly review the practices and policies of the City of San Gabriel.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Direct staff to prepare an ordinance that amends the San Gabriel
  Municipal Code to create a Commission on Human Equity, Access and
  Relations (HEAR Commission); and
  2. Extend the ad hoc sub-committee and continue the appointment of
  Mayor Menchaca and Councilmember Pu for an additional four months,
  with a report to the City Council on the actions of the sub-committee due
  at that time.

  D. MISSION PLAYHOUSE DISCUSSION

  Each year, the City subsidizes the Mission Playhouse operations by an average
  of $735,000. This has resulted in the Mission Playhouse Fund experiencing a
  deficit at June 30, 2020, of over $350,000. As this amount has become
  unsustainable for the General Fund in this economic situation, Staff is
  presenting options for the future operation of the Mission Playhouse.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council discuss this item and provide direction
  to Staff.

 7. PUBLIC COMMENT

MINUTES OF AUGUST 18, 2020
  REGULAR MEETING OF THE SAN GABRIEL CITY COUNCIL

CALL TO ORDER

Mayor Menchaca called the regular meeting of the San Gabriel City Council to order at
6:39 P.M. on Tuesday, August 18, 2020, with all Council Members and staff participating
by teleconference.

CLOSED SESSION REPORT

City Attorney Lemieux reported that in the Closed Session Special Meeting earlier this
evening, on the matter identified as Conference with Legal Counsel – Anticipated
Litigation, the City Council by a unanimous vote agreed to enter into a second Tolling
Agreement with BBK Group and directed staff to execute the agreement.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Vice Mayor Liao.

ROLL CALL

Council Members Present:  Tony Ding, John R. Harrington, Jason Pu, Vice Mayor
  Chin Ho Liao, and Mayor Denise Menchaca.
Council Members Absent:  None.
Staff Members Present:  City Manager Mark Lazzaretto, City Attorney Keith
  Lemieux,  Assistant  City  Manager/Community
  Development Director Arminé Chaparyan, Community
  Services/Interim Mission Playhouse Director Rebecca
  Perez, Police Chief Eugene Harris, Chief City Clerk
  Sharon Clark, Public Works Director/City Engineer Greg
  de Vinck, Fire Chief Steven Wallace, Human
  Resources/Risk Management Director Edward Macias,
  Interim Finance Director Kenneth Louie, and Assistant
  City Clerk Marilyn Bonus.

ANNOUNCEMENTS

Chief City Clerk Clark provided information for the public on how to view the meeting and
submit comments, and how to request meeting agendas.

1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

  City Manager Lazzaretto announced that due to an unfortunate community
  dissemination of incorrect information which resulted in an outpouring of over 300
  comments from the public on New Business Item 6D: Mission Playhouse Discussion,
  he was suggesting two options to the City Council, given the importance of the item
  to the community: 1) To postpone the item to a study session at a special meeting to
  be held on August 25, 2020, with all comments received so far attached to the staff

   report and made available online, and with additional information added to the staff
  report; or 2) Set a time limit for the item, start with reading public comment up until
  the cut-off time, then resume reading comments again at the special meeting.

  Following discussion, a motion was made by Vice Mayor Liao, seconded by Mayor
  Menchaca, to approve the agenda order as amended to postpone New Business Item
  6D to a special meeting to be held on August 25, 2020, at 6:30 P.M.

  Motion carried by a vote of 5-0 as follows:

  AYES:  DING, HARRINGTON, PU, LIAO, MENCHACA
  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN:  NONE
  ABSENT:  NONE

2. PRESENTATIONS

  A. INTRODUCTION OF PLANNING MANAGER SAMANTHA TEWASART

  Presentation was made by Assistant City Manager/Community Development
  Director Arminé Chaparyan.

  B. COVID-19 BRIEFING

  The presentation was made by City Manager Lazzaretto.

3. PUBLIC COMMENT

  Lisa Chen provided comments suggesting features on social media on local
  restaurants and other businesses which are open in the City.

  Camelia Vera, resident, provided comments requesting that speed limits not be
  increased.

  Christine Tureaud provided comments expressing dissatisfaction with various agenda
  item topics.

  Norma provided comments expressing dissatisfaction with the appearance of
  businesses north of the 10 freeway on San Gabriel Boulevard to Las Tunas Drive; and
  suggested a Spanish Mission theme, Gateway, and mix of different eateries for the
  City.

4. CONSENT CALENDAR

  Regarding Item 4D, Council Member Pu requested a stipulation that any future

  A motion was made by Council Member Pu, seconded by Vice Mayor Liao, to approve
  Consent Calendar Items 4A – 4C and 4E – 4G as presented, and Item 4D as amended

  Council.

  Motion approved Consent Calendar Items 4A – 4C and 4E - 4G as presented, and Item
  4D as amended, by a vote of 5-0 as follows:

  AYES:  DING, HARRINGTON, PU, LIAO, MENCHACA
  NOES:  NONE

  A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  The City Council approved:

  1. Minutes of the City Council Special Meeting of August 4, 2020.
  2. Minutes of the City Council Regular Meeting of August 4, 2020.

  B. MATERIAL DEMANDS

  The City Council approved the July 24, 2020, and July 30, 2020, Registers of

  A. MONTHLY BUDGET UPDATE

  The staff presentation was made by Interim Finance Director Ken Louie.

  There was no public comment.

  Discussion included the decline in Charges for Service; Fire Department

  A motion was made by Council Member Pu, seconded by Vice Mayor Liao, to adopt

  Motion approved New Business Item 6A as presented by a vote of 5-0 as follows:

  AYES:  DING, HARRINGTON, PU, LIAO, MENCHACA
  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN:  NONE
  ABSENT:  NONE

  B. CONSIDERATION BY THE CITY COUNCIL TO ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. 20-41
  CONDEMNING AN ATTEMPT BY THE TRUMP ADMINISTRATION TO EXCLUDE
  UNDOCUMENTED PERSONS FROM THE 2020 CENSUS COUNT
  APPORTIONMENT BASE

  The presentation was made by City Attorney Keith Lemieux.

  The following provided comments in opposition to adopting the resolution:
  Norma; Mary Fischer; Linda Parmenter; and Isela Bowles.

  The following provided comments in support of adopting the resolution: Sean
  McMorris, resident; and Jeanne E. Raya, resident and business owner.

  Mayor Menchaca announced that Council Member Harrington had provided a
  redline version of the resolution with his comments to the City Council for
  reference during the meeting.

  Discussion included Council Member Harrington’s requested changes; the
  resolution was vetted by the City Attorney; Census activities; importance of every
  person being counted; the resolution is a statement of policy; transparency of
  public discussion regarding the item; and the importance of using correct legal
  terminology.

  A motion was made by Mayor Menchaca, seconded by Council Member Pu, to
  adopt Resolution No. 20-41, responding to the Trump Administration’s attempt
  to exclude undocumented persons from the 2020 Census Count apportionment
  base.

  Motion approved New Business Item 6B as presented by a vote of 4-1 as follows:

  AYES:  DING, PU, LIAO, MENCHACA
  NOES:  HARRINGTON
  ABSTAIN:  NONE

CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 4 of 6  August 18, 2020
   ABSENT:  NONE

  C. STATUS REPORT FROM THE COMMUNITY EQUALITY AND ENGAGEMENT AD
  HOC SUB-COMMITTEE AND RECOMMENDATION TO CREATE A COMMISION
  ON HUMAN EQUITY, ACCESS AND RELATIONS (THE “HEAR COMMISSION”)

  The presentation was made by City Manager Lazzaretto.

  Norma provided comments in opposition to the creation of the HEAR Commission.

  Charmaine Liccardi provided comments expressing displeasure with Council
  Member Pu and Mayor Menchaca.

  Mary Fischer provided comments stating her opposition to the creation of the
  Commission if it is an attempt to defund the San Gabriel Police Department.

  Alice Wong provided comments requesting transparency in the selection process
  for commissioners.

  Linda Parmenter provided questions and comments about the efficacy of the
  Commission.

  Sean McMorris, resident, and Jeanne E. Raya, resident and business owner,
  provided comments in support of the ordinance and extending the Subcommittee
  for four months.

  Cheryl Cabot, resident, provided comments in support of the creation of the HEAR
  Commission and commended the Subcommittee for its work.

  Chasity Jennings-Nuñez provided comments in support of the HEAR Commission
  and made suggestions as to its duties.

  Mario Pace, resident, commended City staff for posting the Council Meetings to
  YouTube; and requested that meeting audio be put into podcasts, that
  implementation of the HEAR Commission be tabled until the COVID pandemic is
  over, and that the Subcommittee be extended only if new Council Members are
  rotated in and current Council Members rotated out.

  Isela Bowles provided comments expressing concerns about transparency and
  fiscal impact relative to the Subcommittee.

  Discussion included appreciation to staff for their assistance; recent backlash
  against Asian residents; an intergenerational divide in the City; openness among
  stakeholder groups to discuss the issues; examples of past discrimination;
  desirability of all being able to view and/or participate in Subcommittee meetings;
  Subcommittee mission creep; legality of extending the length of the
  Subcommittee’s service; discrimination in the City versus by the City; cautions
  against making appointments to a Commission based on protected-class status;
  that an advisory board is more appropriate in this case than a commission; fiscal
  impact accuracy; getting more community input before making the decision to
  form a commission; benefit of having an independent body to review policies;
  increased transparency through more community involvement on City
  commissions; the Commission as a tool to facilitate communication between
  groups; virtual town hall meetings for more resident participation; and the
  opportunity for more engagement with a four-month extension for the
  Subcommittee.

CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 5 of 6  August 18, 2020
   A motion was made by Council Member Pu, seconded by Mayor Menchaca, to:

  1. Direct staff to prepare an ordinance that amends the San Gabriel Municipal
  Code to create a Commission on Human Equity, Access and Relations (HEAR
  Commission); and
  2. Extend the ad hoc sub-committee and continue the appointment of Mayor
  Menchaca and Councilmember Pu for an additional four months, with a report
  to the City Council on the actions of the sub-committee due at that time.

  Motion approved New Business Item 6C as presented by a vote of 4-1 as follows:

  AYES:  DING, PU, LIAO, MENCHACA
  NOES:  HARRINGTON
  ABSTAIN:  NONE
  ABSENT:  NONE

  D. MISSION PLAYHOUSE DISCUSSION

  This item was postponed to a special meeting to be held on August 25, 2020.

7. PUBLIC COMMENT – None.

8. CITY MANAGER’S REPORT – None.

9. COUNCIL COMMENTS AND CONFERENCE/MEETING REPORTS

  Vice Mayor Liao reported on his attendance at a Grant Writing Workshop hosted by
  Los Angeles County Supervisor Kathryn Barger.

  Council Member Pu and Mayor Menchaca thanked their colleagues who supported
  the formation of the HEAR Commission.

10. CLOSED SESSION – None.

11. ADJOURNMENT

  Mayor Menchaca noted that August 18, 2020, marks the 100 th anniversary of the
  passage of the 19th Amendment, which guaranteed and protected women’s
  constitutional right to vote.

  Mayor Menchaca adjourned the meeting at 9:53 P.M.
